P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, with conditions (Lei Cambial 28/2022 and Aviso 5/GBM/2024). Residents must repatriate service-export receipts within 90 days of receiving the price or fees, through a bank authorised in Mozambique. A share must be converted into meticais on receipt: 30% under Aviso 5/GBM/2024, raised temporarily to 50% in April 2025 for 18 months, and extended by six months from 9 Oct 2026 (Aviso 7/GBM/2026).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes, conditionally. Residents may open a foreign-currency account in Mozambique without Banco de Moçambique authorisation, as a liberalised operation, if they have a proven relationship with abroad or with non-residents that generates foreign-currency flows (e.g. exporters).

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Mozambique (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

P4_paypal.answer: Yes. Mozambique is on PayPal's Payouts list with 'Send, receive, and withdraw'. Repatriation and conversion rules (P1) apply to export receipts.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest: a sole proprietorship (empresa em nome individual), with no formal minimum capital and unlimited liability. It is registered with the Commercial Registry via the one-stop shop (Balcão de Atendimento Único, BAU), in person or online, typically in 7–15 days. Fees were not confirmed.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The NUIT (Número Único de Identificação Tributária), from the Tax Authority (Autoridade Tributária). It is needed to trade, invoice and file taxes, and is among the documents for sole-trader registration.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents are taxed (IRPS) on worldwide income at progressive rates up to 32% (PwC, reviewed Aug 2026). Small taxpayers with annual turnover up to MZN 4m (raised from 2.5m by Law 9/2025, in force 1 Jan 2026) may use ISPC, paid quarterly. Goods sellers pay 3–5% of turnover; technical services pay 12%; liberal professions (e.g. consultants, engineers) pay 15% and may stay in ISPC for at most 5 years.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Standard VAT is 16% (cut from 17% in 2023) (5% reduced on selected supplies). PwC states taxpayers with turnover above MZN 2.5m fall in the standard VAT regime. Exports are mostly zero-rated. Whether the 2026 ISPC ceiling increase (MZN 4m) moved the VAT threshold, and whether exported services are zero-rated, were not established.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: No general data-protection law yet. A Data Protection bill has been submitted to the Assembleia da República (Aug 2026). Meanwhile the Electronic Transactions Law (Lei 3/2017) imposes some data duties, such as naming people responsible for data protection, which many entities do not meet (INTIC). Cybersecurity (Lei 13/2026) and cybercrime (Lei 14/2026) laws were approved in July 2026.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Under the Consumer Protection Law (Lei 22/2009), consumers may withdraw within seven working days of receiving the goods or service when the contract is made off-premises, by correspondence or equivalent means. A right of retraction of seven working days also applies to supplier-initiated off-premises contracts. Whether online sales count as 'correspondence or equivalent' is an interpretation; implementing regulation: Decree 27/2016.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
